proposals: DGCI&S should publish an official 8-digit concordance table with every ITC-HS revision, mapping each retired code to its successor codes and the year of handover, so pairings such as 03061790 to 03061720 for shrimp are official mappings rather than an analyst's inference.

DGCI&S should record the quantity unit for each code by year in its TradeStat files, not once per code, so a switch from tonnes to kilogrammes — found here on codes carrying 14.1% of import value — is visible in the data rather than silently corrupting unit values.

DGCI&S should mark every retired code with its effective retirement date, not just an asterisk on the description, since the asterisk catches only about a quarter of codes that actually stop trading and 46 asterisked codes still carry FY2025-26 value.

DGCI&S should make FY2021-22 commodity-wise 8-digit export values available in the same TradeStat format as other years, so the eight-year series used here does not have to show a gap for a year that is present in the quantity files.

The Ministry of Commerce should publish, with each annual export release, the share of export value booked on codes created or retired since the previous HS revision, so readers know when a headline collapse, like the 95% fall on the old shrimp code, may be recoding rather than trade.
